extracted.intended_audience: EU citizens and stakeholders interested in contributing views to European Commission policy-making
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the different official channels (public consultations, European Citizens’ Initiative, Citizens’ Engagement Platform, children’s platform) through which EU citizens and stakeholders can submit views and engage with the European Commission on policy proposals and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Consultations and feedback (Have Your Say) - single portal
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Consultations and feedback (previously called ‘Have Your Say’) is a single portal for citizens and stakeholders to give their views on the Commission’s initiatives and contribute to the decision-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission is committed to hear citizens and stakeholders’ views on EU laws and policies both when these are being prepared and implemented. Use this portal to submit opinions on upcoming EU policies and on simplifying existing laws. Examples of consultations that fed into decision-making include 'Child protection – integrating systems' and feedback regarding 'EU rules on victims’ rights.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of contributions (what you can comment on)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can 'have a say on upcoming EU policies and on simplifying existing laws' and contribute views both during policy preparation and implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions are sought at different stages (preparation and implementation) and may concern new initiatives or simplification of current rules. Use the portal to indicate what is important to you and to influence policy design and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: European Citizens’ Initiative (ECI) — purpose and signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the European Citizens’ Initiative, EU citizens can call on the European Commission to propose legislation on topics within its competences. An initiative needs to collect at least one million valid signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since its introduction in 2012, over 100 initiatives have been launched and around 18 million EU citizens have supported an initiative. Successful initiatives have influenced Commission legislative proposals on matters such as access to drinking water or setting mandatory targets for reducing the use of chemical pesticides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizens' Engagement Platform — early-stage engagement and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Citizens’ Engagement Platform serves as a dedicated space for citizens to engage in European-level discussions regarding important upcoming EU proposals that affect us all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission seeks opinions at an early stage when drawing up new policy initiatives. The Commission will assess the ideas and proposals put forward, the reactions by other citizens, and consider this assessment when advancing with the formulation of its policy initiatives. Join debates and exchange with other citizens to increase visibility and influence of your views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in specific online debates to inform panels (example: EU Preparedness Union Strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Online debates (e.g., 'Share your ideas for a resilient Europe' / 'Citizens' Engagement Platform: new debate on Preparedness') invite citizens across the EU to contribute ideas and perspectives to inform EU strategies and support Citizens’ Panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debates are open to citizens across the EU and aim to gather ideas that will inform thematic Citizens’ Panels (e.g., the Citizens’ Panel on Preparedness). Contributions should focus on the debate’s theme (for example, ways to strengthen preparedness for future crises such as climate disasters, pandemics, or geopolitical challenges).

rubrics_metrics.name: EU Children's Participation Platform — modalities and involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The EU Children's Participation Platform is a space for dialogue with EU children to bring their voices into EU-level policy making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All EU children can participate in online consultations. Members can also take part in interviews, focus groups, online and offline meetings, and have a say about the direction and implementation of Platform activities, including co-creation of the website and communication aspects. The Platform was set up by the European Commission in cooperation with the European Parliament and civil society organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration of impact — examples and precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions and initiatives may influence Commission proposals and policy outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites concrete examples where public input or Citizens’ Initiatives influenced policy (e.g., child protection consultations, victims’ rights feedback, initiatives leading to proposals on access to drinking water and pesticide reduction targets). Use these precedents to understand potential impact and how to frame submissions to maximise influence.
